notes: None is read as the recast negation on the subject nominal (rule 15); the competing reading gives None to the first אִישׁ and leaves לֹא unrepresented, but the negation must be somewhere and only None carries it.

שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ is split rather than fused, since the ASV spends distinct English on each noun (rule 2); the head on near follows from bearing the ASV's division, and LEV.18.12–13 head the same lexeme on kinswoman where the English differs.
The italic their is added: עֶרְוָה here carries no suffix (rule 18's closing sentence).
